# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

# Architecture
- Clean Architecture, four layers: domain, application (use cases), 
  interface adapters, infrastructure.
- Dependencies point inward only. domain has zero framework imports.
- Package by layer: com.tictactoe.domain, com.tictactoe.application, com.tictactoe.adapters, com.tictactoe.infra
- Build: no build tool — plain `javac`/`java`, Java 17. JUnit 5 (console-standalone) and AssertJ
  are vendored as jars in `lib/` (no dependency manager).
- Tests: JUnit 5 + AssertJ. Run all: `./test.sh`. Run one class: `./test.sh --select-class com.tictactoe.<pkg>.<ClassName>`.
- Run the app: `./run.sh`

# Order
- For every new piece: write the failing test first. Do not write 
  implementation until I've confirmed the test fails for the right reason.
- Build inside-out: domain model + unit tests → use case + tests → 
  adapter + integration test → wire into entry point.

</system-reminder>

2: 
3: A desktop Tic-Tac-Toe game (see the `TicTacToe/` folder), built in Java with a
4: Swing UI. Play two-player locally or against a computer opponent on a
5: configurable board, from the classic 3x3 up to a 10x10 board with a longer
6: line needed to win.
7: 
8: This was developed by Lindsey Shorser with Claude Code on August 12-13, 2026. For a description of the design patterns that were included, see `TicTacToe/DesignPattersn.md`.

11: 
12: ```

17: ## Choosable options
18: 
19: Set on the start screen before each game:
20: 
21: - **Board size** — 2x2 up to 10x10.
22: - **Win length** — how many marks in a row are needed to win; capped at the
23:   board size.
24: - **Game mode** — Two Players (pass and play locally) or vs Computer.
25: - **AI difficulty** *(vs Computer only)* — Easy (random moves), Medium
26:   (takes an obvious win or block when available), or Difficult (plays a
27:   full lookahead search and rarely loses).
28: 
29: ## Toggle-able options
30: 
31: Independent on/off switches, also on the start screen:
32: 
33: - **Win effects** — confetti, fireworks, and twinkling X's & O's each play
34:   when a game is won; toggle any combination on or off.
35: - **Night Mode** — switches the whole UI between a light "Day Mode" and a
36:   dark "Night Mode" palette, live, without needing to restart.

I'll pick two from `GameControllerTest` that best show the Mockito approach — an async one and the error-handling one.

## 1. `onCellClickedOnOccupiedCellShowsErrorAndDoesNotChangeBoard`

`src/test/java/com/tictactoe/adapters/GameControllerTest.java:115`

```java
GameView view = mock(GameView.class);
GameController controller = newController(view);        // uses immediateScheduler()
controller.onStartGameRequested(twoPlayerRequest());
controller.onCellClicked(0, 0);                          // X places at (0,0)
BoardViewModel boardAfterFirstMove = lastBoard(view);    // capture board after move

controller.onCellClicked(0, 0);                          // try to place on occupied cell

assertThat(lastError(view)).isNotNull();
assertThat(lastBoard(view)).isEqualTo(boardAfterFirstMove);
```

What it verifies: clicking an already-occupied cell must (a) surface an error message to the UI and (b) leave the board untouched.

How it works: `GameView` is a Mockito mock (the presenter boundary). `lastBoard(view)` captures the last `BoardViewModel` passed to `view.displayBoard(...)` via an `ArgumentCaptor`, and `lastError(view)` captures the last `String` passed to `view.displayError(...)`. So the assertions check the **real effects** the controller emitted, not just that a method was called. `boardAfterFirstMove` is captured *before* the second click, so comparing it to the board after the click proves nothing changed — this is the "assert on the real effect" style AGENTS.md calls for.

## 2. `onCellClickedInVsAiModeDoesNotBlockUntilTheAiMoveCompletes`

`src/test/java/com/tictactoe/adapters/GameControllerTest.java:228`

```java
GameView view = mock(GameView.class);
CapturingScheduler scheduler = new CapturingScheduler();
GameController controller = newController(view, scheduler.scheduler);
controller.onStartGameRequested(new NewGameRequest(CONFIG_3X3, GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI, Optional.of(AiDifficulty.MEDIUM)));

controller.onCellClicked(0, 0);

// human move is rendered immediately; the AI move hasn't run yet
assertThat(cellAt(lastBoard(view), 0, 0)).isEqualTo(CellSymbol.X);
assertThat(cellAt(lastBoard(view), 1, 1)).isEqualTo(CellSymbol.EMPTY);

scheduler.runNextBackgroundTask();
scheduler.runNextUiTask();

assertThat(cellAt(lastBoard(view), 1, 1)).isEqualTo(CellSymbol.O);
```

What it verifies: in vs-AI mode, the human move must render **immediately** while the AI move is dispatched asynchronously in the background, so the UI doesn't block while the AI thinks.

How it works: instead of the synchronous scheduler, this uses `CapturingScheduler` — a Mockito-mocked `UiScheduler` whose `runInBackground`/`runOnUiThread` are stubbed (via `doAnswer`) to **store** the submitted `Runnable`s in a queue rather than run them. So right after `onCellClicked`, the human's `X` is already on the board (that part is synchronous), but `(1,1)` is still `EMPTY` because the AI task is sitting in the queue. Then `runNextBackgroundTask()` + `runNextUiTask()` manually drain the queue, simulating the AI thread completing and posting back to the UI thread, after which `O` appears at `(1,1)`. This lets the test control timing deterministically without real threads.

Both tests use Mockito for the `GameView`/`UiScheduler` boundaries (the two collaborators) while keeping the real `GameController` and domain logic — the pattern AGENTS.md prescribes.

Here's a grounded proposal, based on the actual dependencies in the code.

## Recommendation: one `game` capability + a `framework` shell

This app is a single cohesive feature — "play a Tic-Tac-Toe match" — so it maps to **one capability**, not several. Making AI a *peer* capability creates a package cycle: `GameController`/`RequestAiMoveUseCase` need the AI, while every `AiStrategy` operates on `Board`/`GameState`/`GameConfig`. Splitting them into `game/` and `ai/` would force them to depend on each other.

Instead, `ai/` becomes a domain sub-package inside `game/`, and the Swing app is the top-level `framework/` delivery mechanism (AGENTS.md explicitly lists `framework/` as top-level, like `data_access/`/`app/`).

### Target layout

```
com.tictactoe
└── game/                                # capability: play a match
    ├── domain/                          # pure rules + shared types
    │   ├── Board, GameState, GameConfig, GameMode, GameStatus
    │   ├── Mark, Position, InProgress, Win, Draw
    │   ├── LineGenerator, WinChecker, AiDifficulty
    │   └── exception/
    │       ├── InvalidGameConfigException, InvalidMoveException
    ├── ai/                              # sub-feature: computer opponent (depends on domain)
    │   ├── AiStrategy, RandomAiStrategy, EasyAiStrategy, MinimaxAiStrategy
    │   ├── BoardEvaluator, MoveOrderer, AiStrategyFactory
    ├── use_case/
    │   ├── StartNewGameUseCase
    │   ├── MakeHumanMoveUseCase
    │   └── RequestAiMoveUseCase
    ├── NewGameRequest                    # application DTO (input for start-game)
    └── adapters/                        # presentation ports for this capability
        ├── GameController, GameControllerBuilder, GameView
        ├── GameViewDecorator, WinEffectGameView, GameViewModelMapper
        ├── NewGameRequestFactory, UiScheduler   # port; impl in framework
        └── viewmodel/
            ├── BoardViewModel, CellViewModel, CellSymbol
            ├── GameOutcomeKind, StatusViewModel
└── framework/                           # delivery mechanism (top-level, not a capability)
    ├── Main
    ├── SwingUiScheduler                 # implements game/adapters.UiScheduler
    └── ui/
        ├── MainFrame, BoardPanel, SetupPanel, StatusPanel
        ├── EffectOverlayPanel, Theme
```

### Dependency direction (clean, acyclic)
- `game/domain` ← `game/ai` ← `game/use_case` ← `game/adapters`
- `game/adapters` ← `framework` (framework implements the `UiScheduler` port and wires `Main`)
- Nothing in `game` knows about Swing.

### What moves where
| Current (by layer) | New |
|---|---|
| `domain/*`, `domain/ai/*`, `domain/exception/*` | `game/domain/*`, `game/ai/*`, `game/domain/exception/*` |
| `application/usecase/*` | `game/use_case/*` |
| `application/NewGameRequest`, `AiStrategyFactory` | `game/NewGameRequest`, `game/ai/AiStrategyFactory` |
| `adapters/*`, `adapters/viewmodel/*` | `game/adapters/*`, `game/adapters/viewmodel/*` |
| `infra/Main`, `infra/ui/*` | `framework/Main`, `framework/ui/*` |
| tests | mirror packages under `src/test/java/com/tictactoe/game/**` and `framework/**` |

### Notes baked into this pass
- Renames `usecase` → `use_case` (AGENTS.md naming).
- Satisfies the `CommonXxxFactory` convention: introduce a small `GameStateFactory` (or `GameStateBuilder`) for aggregate construction, replacing the static `GameState.newGame(...)` the controllers/use cases call.
- Deletes `com.tictactoe.*` remnants of `application`/`infra`; `git mv` preserves history.

### Alternative (only if you want `ai` as a true peer capability)
Put `AiStrategy` in terms of a narrow board interface the game exposes so `ai/` no longer imports `game/domain` — then `ai/` and `game/` are peers with `game → ai` one-way. This is more "pure" but over-engineered for 3 strategies and adds an abstraction layer.

invocation.<Runnable>getArgument(0).run();\n            return null;\n        }).when(scheduler).runInBackground(any());\n        doAnswer(invocation -> {\n            invocation.<Runnable>getArgument(0).run();\n            return null;\n        }).when(scheduler).runOnUiThread(any());\n        return scheduler;\n    }\n\n    private static final class      return null;\n            }).when(scheduler).runInBackground(any());\n            doAnswer(invocation -> {\n                uiTasks.add(invocation.getArgument(0));\n                return null;\n            }).when(scheduler).runOnUiThread(any());\n        }\n\n        private void runNextBackgroundTask() {\n            backgroundTasks.remove(0).run();\n        }\n\n        private void  controller.onCellClicked(2, 2);\n\n        assertThat(lastBoard(view)).isEqualTo(boardAfterWin);\n        verify(view, never()).displayError(any());\n    }\n\n    @Test\n    void now maps to EasyAiStrategy; X at (0,0) leaves no win/block available yet,\n        // so it falls back to the center of the (odd-sized) empty board.\n        assertThat(cellAt(lastBoard(view), 0, human move is rendered immediately; the AI move hasn't run yet\n        assertThat(cellAt(lastBoard(view), 0, 0)).isEqualTo(CellSymbol.X);\n        assertThat(cellAt(lastBoard(view), 1, 1)).isEqualTo(CellSymbol.EMPTY);\n\n        scheduler.runNextBackgroundTask();\n        scheduler.runNextUiTask();\n\n        assertThat(cellAt(lastBoard(view), 1, 1)).isEqualTo(CellSymbol.O);\n controller.onStartGameRequested(twoPlayerRequest());\n\n        // X O X\n        // X X O\n        // O X O\n        controller.onCellClicked(0, 0); // X\n        controller.onCellClicked(0, 1); // package account.signup.use_case;

import user.User;
import user.UserFactory;

/**
 * The Signup Interactor.
 */
public class SignupInteractor implements SignupInputBoundary {
    private final SignupUserDataAccessInterface userDataAccessObject;
    private final SignupOutputBoundary userPresenter;
    private final UserFactory userFactory;

    public SignupInteractor(SignupUserDataAccessInterface signupDataAccessInterface,
                            SignupOutputBoundary signupOutputBoundary,
                            UserFactory userFactory) {
        this.userDataAccessObject = signupDataAccessInterface;
        this.userPresenter = signupOutputBoundary;
        this.userFactory = userFactory;
    }

    @Override
    public void execute(SignupInputData signupInputData) {
        if (userDataAccessObject.existsByName(signupInputData.getUsername())) {
            userPresenter.prepareFailView("User already exists.");
        }
        else if (!signupInputData.getPassword().equals(signupInputData.getRepeatPassword())) {
            userPresenter.prepareFailView("Passwords don't match.");
        }
        else {
            final User user = userFactory.create(signupInputData.getUsername(), signupInputData.getPassword());
            userDataAccessObject.save(user);

            final SignupOutputData signupOutputData = new SignupOutputData(user.getName(), false);
            userPresenter.prepareSuccessView(signupOutputData);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void switchToLoginView() {
        userPresenter.switchToLoginView();
    }
}

package account.signup;

import account.signup.use_case.SignupInputBoundary;
import account.signup.use_case.SignupInputData;

/**
 * Controller for the Signup Use Case.
 */
public class SignupController {

    private final SignupInputBoundary userSignupUseCaseInteractor;

    public SignupController(SignupInputBoundary userSignupUseCaseInteractor) {
        this.userSignupUseCaseInteractor = userSignupUseCaseInteractor;
    }

    /**
     * Executes the Signup Use Case.
     * @param username the username to sign up
     * @param password1 the password
     * @param password2 the password repeated
     */
    public void execute(String username, String password1, String password2) {
        final SignupInputData signupInputData = new SignupInputData(
                username, password1, password2);

        userSignupUseCaseInteractor.execute(signupInputData);
    }

    /**
     * Executes the "switch to LoginView" Use Case.
     */
    public void switchToLoginView() {
        userSignupUseCaseInteractor.switchToLoginView();
    }
}

package account.signup;

import framework.ViewManagerModel;
import authentication.login.LoginState;
import authentication.login.LoginViewModel;
import account.signup.use_case.SignupOutputBoundary;
import account.signup.use_case.SignupOutputData;

/**
 * The Presenter for the Signup Use Case.
 */
public class SignupPresenter implements SignupOutputBoundary {

    private final SignupViewModel signupViewModel;
    private final LoginViewModel loginViewModel;
    private final ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel;

    public SignupPresenter(ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel,
                           SignupViewModel signupViewModel,
                           LoginViewModel loginViewModel) {
        this.viewManagerModel = viewManagerModel;
        this.signupViewModel = signupViewModel;
        this.loginViewModel = loginViewModel;
    }

    @Override
    public void prepareSuccessView(SignupOutputData response) {
        // On success, switch to the login view.
        final LoginState loginState = loginViewModel.getState();
        loginState.setUsername(response.getUsername());
        this.loginViewModel.setState(loginState);
        loginViewModel.firePropertyChanged();

        viewManagerModel.setState(loginViewModel.getViewName());
        viewManagerModel.firePropertyChanged();
    }

    @Override
    public void prepareFailView(String error) {
        final SignupState signupState = signupViewModel.getState();
        signupState.setUsernameError(error);
        signupViewModel.firePropertyChanged();
    }

    @Override
    public void switchToLoginView() {
        viewManagerModel.setState(loginViewModel.getViewName());
        viewManagerModel.firePropertyChanged();
    }
}

package account.signup;
import framework.LabelTextPanel;



import javax.swing.*;
import javax.swing.event.DocumentEvent;
import javax.swing.event.DocumentListener;
import java.awt.*;
import java.awt.event.ActionEvent;
import java.awt.event.ActionListener;
import java.beans.PropertyChangeEvent;
import java.beans.PropertyChangeListener;

/**
 * The View for the Signup Use Case.
 */
public class SignupView extends JPanel implements ActionListener, PropertyChangeListener {
    private final String viewName = "sign up";

    private final SignupViewModel signupViewModel;
    private final JTextField usernameInputField = new JTextField(15);
    private final JPasswordField passwordInputField = new JPasswordField(15);
    private final JPasswordField repeatPasswordInputField = new JPasswordField(15);
    private SignupController signupController = null;

    private final JButton signUp;
    private final JButton cancel;
    private final JButton toLogin;

    public SignupView(SignupViewModel signupViewModel) {
        this.signupViewModel = signupViewModel;
        signupViewModel.addPropertyChangeListener(this);

        final JLabel title = new JLabel(SignupViewModel.TITLE_LABEL);
        title.setAlignmentX(Component.CENTER_ALIGNMENT);

        final LabelTextPanel usernameInfo = new LabelTextPanel(
                new JLabel(SignupViewModel.USERNAME_LABEL), usernameInputField);
        final LabelTextPanel passwordInfo = new LabelTextPanel(
                new JLabel(SignupViewModel.PASSWORD_LABEL), passwordInputField);
        final LabelTextPanel repeatPasswordInfo = new LabelTextPanel(
                new JLabel(SignupViewModel.REPEAT_PASSWORD_LABEL), repeatPasswordInputField);

        final JPanel buttons = new JPanel();
        toLogin = new JButton(SignupViewModel.TO_LOGIN_BUTTON_LABEL);
        buttons.add(toLogin);
        signUp = new JButton(SignupViewModel.SIGNUP_BUTTON_LABEL);
        buttons.add(signUp);
        cancel = new JButton(SignupViewModel.CANCEL_BUTTON_LABEL);
        buttons.add(cancel);

        signUp.addActionListener(
                // This creates an anonymous subclass of ActionListener and instantiates it.
                new ActionListener() {
                    public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent evt) {
                        if (evt.getSource().equals(signUp)) {
                            final SignupState currentState = signupViewModel.getState();

                            signupController.execute(
                                    currentState.getUsername(),
                                    currentState.getPassword(),
                                    currentState.getRepeatPassword()
                            );
                        }
                    }
                }
        );

        toLogin.addActionListener(
                new ActionListener() {
                    public void actionPerformed(ActionEvent evt) {
                        signupController.switchToLoginView();
                    }
                }
        );

        cancel.addActionListener(this);

        addUsernameListener();
        addPasswordListener();
        addRepeatPasswordListener();

        this.setLayout(new BoxLayout(this, BoxLayout.Y_AXIS));

        this.add(title);
        this.add(usernameInfo);
        this.add(passwordInfo);
        this.add(repeatPasswordInfo);
        this.add(buttons);
    }

    private void addUsernameListener() {
        usernameInputField.getDocument().addDocumentListener(new DocumentListener() {

            private void documentListenerHelper() {
                final SignupState currentState = signupViewModel.getState();
                currentState.setUsername(usernameInputField.getText());
                signupViewModel.setState(currentState);
            }

            @Override

package framework;


import javax.swing.*;
import java.awt.*;
import java.beans.PropertyChangeEvent;
import java.beans.PropertyChangeListener;

/**
 * The View Manager for the program. It listens for property change events
 * in the ViewManagerModel and updates which View should be visible.
 */
public class ViewManager implements PropertyChangeListener {
    private final CardLayout cardLayout;
    private final JPanel views;
    private final ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel;

    public ViewManager(JPanel views, CardLayout cardLayout, ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel) {
        this.views = views;
        this.cardLayout = cardLayout;
        this.viewManagerModel = viewManagerModel;
        this.viewManagerModel.addPropertyChangeListener(this);
    }

    @Override
    public void propertyChange(PropertyChangeEvent evt) {
        if (evt.getPropertyName().equals("state")) {
            final String viewModelName = (String) evt.getNewValue();
            cardLayout.show(views, viewModelName);
        }
    }
}

package framework;

import java.beans.PropertyChangeListener;
import java.beans.PropertyChangeSupport;

/**
 * The ViewModel for our CA implementation.
 * This class delegates work to a PropertyChangeSupport object for
 * managing the property change events.
 *
 * @param <T> The type of state object contained in the model.
 */
public class ViewModel<T> {

    private final String viewName;

    private final PropertyChangeSupport support = new PropertyChangeSupport(this);

    private T state;

    public ViewModel(String viewName) {
        this.viewName = viewName;
    }

    public String getViewName() {
        return this.viewName;
    }

    public T getState() {
        return this.state;
    }

    public void setState(T state) {
        this.state = state;
    }

    /**
     * Fires a property changed event for the state of this ViewModel.
     */
    public void firePropertyChanged() {
        this.support.firePropertyChange("state", null, this.state);
    }

    /**
     * Fires a property changed event for the state of this ViewModel, which
     * allows the user to specify a different propertyName. This can be useful
     * when a class is listening for multiple kinds of property changes.
     * <p/>
     * For example, the ChangePasswordView listens for two kinds of property changes;
     * it can use the property name to distinguish which property has changed.
     * @param propertyName the label for the property that was changed
     */
    public void firePropertyChanged(String propertyName) {
        this.support.firePropertyChange(propertyName, null, this.state);
    }

    /**
     * Adds a PropertyChangeListener to this ViewModel.
     * @param listener The PropertyChangeListener to be added
     */
    public void addPropertyChangeListener(PropertyChangeListener listener) {
        this.support.addPropertyChangeListener(listener);
    }
}

package app;

import data_access.DBUserDataAccessObject;
import user.CommonUserFactory;
import user.UserFactory;
import framework.ViewManagerModel;
import account.change_password.ChangePasswordController;
import account.change_password.ChangePasswordPresenter;
import account.change_password.ChangePasswordViewModel;
import authentication.login.LoginController;
import authentication.login.LoginPresenter;
import authentication.login.LoginViewModel;
import account.signup.SignupController;
import account.signup.SignupPresenter;
import account.signup.SignupViewModel;
import account.change_password.use_case.ChangePasswordInputBoundary;
import account.change_password.use_case.ChangePasswordInteractor;
import account.change_password.use_case.ChangePasswordOutputBoundary;
import authentication.login.use_case.LoginInputBoundary;
import authentication.login.use_case.LoginInteractor;
import authentication.login.use_case.LoginOutputBoundary;
import account.signup.use_case.SignupInputBoundary;
import account.signup.use_case.SignupInteractor;
import account.signup.use_case.SignupOutputBoundary;
import account.change_password.ChangePasswordView;
import authentication.login.LoginView;
import account.signup.SignupView;
import framework.ViewManager;

import javax.swing.*;
import java.awt.*;

public class AppBuilder {
    private final JPanel cardPanel = new JPanel();
    private final CardLayout cardLayout = new CardLayout();
    final UserFactory userFactory = new CommonUserFactory();
    final ViewManagerModel viewManagerModel = new ViewManagerModel();
    ViewManager viewManager = new ViewManager(cardPanel, cardLayout, viewManagerModel);

    final DBUserDataAccessObject userDataAccessObject = new DBUserDataAccessObject(new CommonUserFactory());

    private SignupView signupView;
    private SignupViewModel signupViewModel;
    private LoginViewModel loginViewModel;
    private ChangePasswordViewModel changePasswordViewModel;
    private ChangePasswordView changePasswordView;
    private LoginView loginView;

    public AppBuilder() {
        cardPanel.setLayout(cardLayout);
    }

    public AppBuilder addSignupView() {
        signupViewModel = new SignupViewModel();
        signupView = new SignupView(signupViewModel);
        cardPanel.add(signupView, signupView.getViewName());
        return this;
    }

    public AppBuilder addLoginView() {
        loginViewModel = new LoginViewModel();
        loginView = new LoginView(loginViewModel);
        cardPanel.add(loginView, loginView.getViewName());
        return this;
    }

    public AppBuilder addChangePasswordView() {
        changePasswordViewModel = new ChangePasswordViewModel();
        changePasswordView = new ChangePasswordView(changePasswordViewModel);
        cardPanel.add(changePasswordView, changePasswordView.getViewName());
        return this;
    }

    public AppBuilder addSignupUseCase() {
        final SignupOutputBoundary signupOutputBoundary = new SignupPresenter(viewManagerModel,
                signupViewModel, loginViewModel);
        final SignupInputBoundary userSignupInteractor = new SignupInteractor(
                userDataAccessObject, signupOutputBoundary, userFactory);

        SignupController controller = new SignupController(userSignupInteractor);
        signupView.setSignupController(controller);
        return this;
    }

    public AppBuilder addLoginUseCase() {
        final LoginOutputBoundary loginOutputBoundary = new LoginPresenter(viewManagerModel,
                changePasswordViewModel, loginViewModel);
        final LoginInputBoundary loginInteractor = new LoginInteractor(
                userDataAccessObject, loginOutputBoundary);

        LoginController loginController = new LoginController(loginInteractor);
        loginView.setLoginController(loginController);
        return this;
    }

    public AppBuilder addChangePasswordUseCase() {
        final ChangePasswordOutputBoundary changePasswordOutputBoundary = new ChangePasswordPresenter(viewManagerModel,
                changePasswordViewModel);

        final UserFactory userFactory = new CommonUserFactory();

        final ChangePasswordInputBoundary changePasswordInteractor =
                new ChangePasswordInteractor(userDataAccessObject, changePasswordOutputBoundary, userFactory);

        ChangePasswordController changePasswordController = new ChangePasswordController(changePasswordInteractor);
        changePasswordView.setChangePasswordController(changePasswordController);
        return this;
    }

    public JFrame build() {
        final JFrame application = new JFrame("Login Example");
        application.setDefaultCloseOperation(WindowConstants.EXIT_ON_CLOSE);

        application.add(cardPanel);

        viewManagerModel.setState(signupView.getViewName());
        viewManagerModel.firePropertyChanged();

        return application;
    }


}

package data_access;

import user.User;
import account.change_password.use_case.ChangePasswordUserDataAccessInterface;
import authentication.login.use_case.LoginUserDataAccessInterface;
import account.signup.use_case.SignupUserDataAccessInterface;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * In-memory implementation of the DAO for storing user data. This implementation does
 * NOT persist data between runs of the program.
 */
public class InMemoryUserDataAccessObject implements SignupUserDataAccessInterface,
                                                     LoginUserDataAccessInterface,
                                                     ChangePasswordUserDataAccessInterface {

    private final Map<String, User> users = new HashMap<>();

    private String currentUser;

    @Override
    public boolean existsByName(String identifier) {
        return users.containsKey(identifier);
    }

    @Override
    public void save(User user) {
        users.put(user.getName(), user);
    }

    @Override
    public User get(String username) {
        return users.get(username);
    }

    @Override
    public void changePassword(User user) {
        // Replace the old entry with the new password
        users.put(user.getName(), user);
    }

}

package account.signup.use_case;

import user.CommonUserFactory;
import user.User;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;
import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertFalse;
import static org.mockito.ArgumentMatchers.any;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.never;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.verify;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.when;

/**
 * Test cases for the Signup Interactor.
 */
@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
public class SignupInteractorTest {

    @Mock
    private SignupUserDataAccessInterface userDataAccessObject;
    @Mock
    private SignupOutputBoundary userPresenter;

    private SignupInteractor signupInteractor;

    /**
     * Sets up the interactor with the mocked data access and presenter.
     */
    @BeforeEach
    void setUp() {
        signupInteractor = new SignupInteractor(userDataAccessObject, userPresenter, new CommonUserFactory());
    }

    /**
     * Tests that the interactor reports a failure when the username already exists.
     */
    @Test
    void signupUserAlreadyExists_ShowsFailureView() {
        when(userDataAccessObject.existsByName("Paul")).thenReturn(true);

        final SignupInputData inputData = new SignupInputData("Paul", "password", "password");
        signupInteractor.execute(inputData);

        verify(userPresenter).prepareFailView("User already exists.");
        verify(userPresenter, never()).prepareSuccessView(any());
        verify(userDataAccessObject, never()).save(any());
    }

    /**
     * Tests that the interactor reports a failure when the passwords do not match.
     */
    @Test
    void signupPasswordsDoNotMatch_ShowsFailureView() {
        when(userDataAccessObject.existsByName("Paul")).thenReturn(false);

        final SignupInputData inputData = new SignupInputData("Paul", "password", "different");
        signupInteractor.execute(inputData);

        verify(userPresenter).prepareFailView("Passwords don't match.");
        verify(userPresenter, never()).prepareSuccessView(any());
        verify(userDataAccessObject, never()).save(any());
    }

    /**
     * Tests that the interactor creates and saves a user and shows the success view.
     */
    @Test
    void signupSuccess_CreatesUserAndShowsSuccessView() {
        when(userDataAccessObject.existsByName("Paul")).thenReturn(false);

        final SignupInputData inputData = new SignupInputData("Paul", "password", "password");
        signupInteractor.execute(inputData);

        final ArgumentCaptor<User> savedUserCaptor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(User.class);
        verify(userDataAccessObject).save(savedUserCaptor.capture());
        assertEquals("Paul", savedUserCaptor.getValue().getName());
        assertEquals("password", savedUserCaptor.getValue().getPassword());

        final ArgumentCaptor<SignupOutputData> outputDataCaptor =
                ArgumentCaptor.forClass(SignupOutputData.class);
        verify(userPresenter).prepareSuccessView(outputDataCaptor.capture());
        final SignupOutputData outputData = outputDataCaptor.getValue();
        assertEquals("Paul", outputData.getUsername());
        assertFalse(outputData.isUseCaseFailed());
        verify(userPresenter, never()).prepareFailView(any());
    }

    /**
     * Tests that switchToLoginView delegates to the presenter.
     */
    @Test
    void switchToLoginView_DelegatesToPresenter() {
        signupInteractor.switchToLoginView();

        verify(userPresenter).switchToLoginView();
    }
}

## CAWithBuilder's structure (the patterns it teaches)

**Per-capability component set** — every feature (`account/signup`, `account/change_password`, `authentication/login`) is self-contained:
- `use_case/` → `XxxInputBoundary`, `XxxInputData`, `XxxInteractor` (implements the boundary), `XxxOutputBoundary`, `XxxOutputData`, `XxxUserDataAccessInterface`
- capability root → `XxxController`, `XxxPresenter`, `XxxState` (mutable UI bean), `XxxViewModel` (extends `framework.ViewModel<T>`), `XxxView` (Swing panel)

**Boundary-driven production code** — controllers hold the `InputBoundary` interface, interactors hold `UserDataAccessInterface` + `OutputBoundary` + `UserFactory` (all interfaces). Only `AppBuilder` instantiates concretes.

**Shared entity + factory** — `user/User` + `user/UserFactory` interfaces, `user/CommonUser` + `user/CommonUserFactory` implementations.

**Framework** — `framework.ViewModel<T>` (PropertyChangeSupport + state + `firePropertyChanged`), `ViewManagerModel` (navigation state), `ViewManager` (switches CardLayout cards), `LabelTextPanel`.

**Composition** — `app/AppBuilder` (fluent `addSignupUseCase()` etc.) + `app/Main`. No `com.*` prefix — packages are `account`, `user`, `framework`, `app`, `data_access`.

**Tests** — interactor-only, `@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension)`, `@Mock` DAO + presenter, `@BeforeEach` builds the interactor, `ArgumentCaptor` asserts on real effects, `Method_Condition_Expectation` names.

## How tictactoe currently differs

| CAWithBuilder | tictactoe (current) |
|---|---|
| `account.signup` (no prefix) | `com.tictactoe.game.adapters` (com prefix) |
| InputBoundary/InputData/OutputBoundary/OutputData per use case | bare `*UseCase` classes, no boundaries |
| Controller depends on `InputBoundary` interface | `GameController` depends on concrete `*UseCase` classes |
| Presenter + `ViewModel<T>` + mutable `State` bean + `View` | `GameViewModelMapper` → immutable `viewmodel/*`, `GameView` interface |
| `framework.ViewModel`/`ViewManager`/`ViewManagerModel` | none (no card navigation) |
| `AppBuilder` wires everything | `Main` + `GameControllerBuilder` wire |
| `user/CommonUser` + `CommonUserFactory` | `GameState` aggregate + `GameStateFactory` |
| DAO `data_access` impls | no persistence layer |

Good news: we already match on **package-by-capability**, **`use_case`** spelling, and **Mockito interactor-style tests** (from the earlier passes).

## Proposed updates (grouped by theme)

**1. Package naming** — drop `com.tictactoe`, use top-level `game`, `framework`, `app`. (`game.domain`, `game.use_case`, `game.adapters`, `framework.ui`.)

**2. Use-case boundaries** — turn the three `*UseCase` classes into the full boundary set: `StartNewGame{InputBoundary,InputData,Interactor,OutputBoundary,OutputData}`, same for `MakeHumanMove`, `RequestAiMove`. `GameController` depends on the boundaries (interfaces), not concretes.

**3. Presenter / State / ViewModel / View** — introduce a `GamePresenter` (implements the output boundaries), a mutable UI `GameState` bean, and a `GameViewModel extends framework.ViewModel<GameState>`; convert `GameView` into the Swing `View`. This splits today's conflated `GameViewModelMapper` + `viewmodel/*` into the CA MVVM-style components. Adopt `framework.ViewModel<T>`, `ViewManagerModel`, `ViewManager`, `LabelTextPanel`.

**4. AppBuilder** — move composition out of `Main`/`GameControllerBuilder` into `app/AppBuilder` (fluent `addGameView()`, `addGameUseCase()`), with `app/Main` as entry.

**5. data_access** — today nothing is persisted (game lives in the controller). This is **N/A** unless you want to add persistence/high-scores. I'd skip it.

**6. Tests** — keep the interactor-focused Mockito tests but retarget them at the new boundaries (`*Interactor` tested with `@Mock` DAO + presenter), matching CAWithBuilder's test shape exactly.

**7. Shared entity factory** — already satisfied (`GameStateFactory`); rename to follow the `CommonXxx` convention only if you want strict parity.

package com.tictactoe.game.use_case;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThatThrownBy;

import com.tictactoe.game.domain.GameConfig;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.GameState;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.Mark;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.Position;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.exception.InvalidMoveException;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class MakeHumanMoveUseCaseTest {

    private static final GameConfig CONFIG_3X3 = new GameConfig(3, 3);
    private final MakeHumanMoveUseCase useCase = new MakeHumanMoveUseCase();

    @Test
    void executeAppliesValidMoveAndReturnsUpdatedGameState() {
        GameState state = GameState.newGame(CONFIG_3X3);

        GameState next = useCase.execute(state, new Position(0, 0));

        assertThat(next.board().get(new Position(0, 0))).contains(Mark.X);
        assertThat(next.currentTurn()).isEqualTo(Mark.O);
    }

    @Test
    void executeThrowsWhenGameAlreadyOver() {
        GameState state = GameState.newGame(CONFIG_3X3)
            .applyMove(new Position(0, 0)) // X
            .applyMove(new Position(1, 0)) // O
            .applyMove(new Position(0, 1)) // X
            .applyMove(new Position(1, 1)) // O
            .applyMove(new Position(0, 2)); // X wins

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> useCase.execute(state, new Position(2, 2)))
            .isInstanceOf(InvalidMoveException.class);
    }

    @Test
    void executeThrowsWhenCellOccupied() {
        GameState state = GameState.newGame(CONFIG_3X3).applyMove(new Position(0, 0));

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> useCase.execute(state, new Position(0, 0)))
            .isInstanceOf(InvalidMoveException.class);
    }
}

class RequestAiMoveUseCaseTest {

    private static final GameConfig CONFIG_3X3 = new GameConfig(3, 3);
    private final RequestAiMoveUseCase useCase = new RequestAiMoveUseCase();
    private final AiStrategy fixedMoveStrategy = new AiStrategy() {
        @Override
        public Position selectMove(Board board, GameConfig config, Mark aiMark) {
            return new Position(1, 1);
        }
    };

    @Test
    void executeAsksStrategyForMoveAndAppliesIt() {
        GameState state = GameState.newGame(CONFIG_3X3);

        GameState next = useCase.execute(state, fixedMoveStrategy);

        assertThat(next.board().get(new Position(1, 1))).contains(Mark.X);
        assertThat(next.currentTurn()).isEqualTo(Mark.O);
    }

    @Test
    void executeThrowsWhenGameAlreadyOver() {
        GameState state = GameState.newGame(CONFIG_3X3)
            .applyMove(new Position(0, 0)) // X
            .applyMove(new Position(1, 0)) // O
            .applyMove(new Position(0, 1)) // X
            .applyMove(new Position(1, 1)) // O
            .applyMove(new Position(0, 2)); // X wins

        assertThatThrownBy(() -> useCase.execute(state, fixedMoveStrategy))
            .isInstanceOf(InvalidMoveException.class);
    }
}

class StartNewGameUseCaseTest {

    private final StartNewGameUseCase useCase = new StartNewGameUseCase();

    @Test
    void executeReturnsGameStateWithConfiguredBoardSizeAndWinLength() {
        GameConfig config = new GameConfig(4, 3);
        NewGameRequest request = new NewGameRequest(config, GameMode.TWO_PLAYER, Optional.empty());

        GameState state = useCase.execute(request);

        assertThat(state.config()).isEqualTo(config);
        assertThat(state.board().emptyPositions()).hasSize(16);
    }

    @Test
    void executeStartsWithEmptyBoardXsTurnAndInProgressStatus() {
        GameConfig config = new GameConfig(3, 3);
        NewGameRequest request = new NewGameRequest(config, GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI, Optional.empty());

        GameState state = useCase.execute(request);

        assertThat(state.currentTurn()).isEqualTo(Mark.X);
        assertThat(state.status()).isInstanceOf(InProgress.class);
    }
}

```java
package com.tictactoe.game.use_case;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.GameStateFactory;
public final class StartNewGameInteractor implements StartNewGameInputBoundary {
    private final StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter;
    public StartNewGameInteractor(StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter) { this.presenter = presenter; }
    @Override public void execute(StartNewGameInputData inputData) {
        presenter.prepareSuccessView(new StartNewGameOutputData(
            GameStateFactory.newGame(inputData.request().config())));
    }
}
```

**MakeHumanMoveInputData** (record): (GameState state, Position position)
**MakeHumanMoveInputBoundary**: void execute(MakeHumanMoveInputData)
**MakeHumanMoveOutputData** (record): (GameState updatedState)
**MakeHumanMoveOutputBoundary**: prepareSuccessView(MakeHumanMoveOutputData), prepareFailView(String)
**MakeHumanMoveInteractor**:
```java
public void execute(MakeHumanMoveInputData inputData) {
    try {
        GameState updated = inputData.state().applyMove(inputData.position());
        presenter.prepareSuccessView(new MakeHumanMoveOutputData(updated));
    } catch (InvalidMoveException e) {
        presenter.prepareFailView(e.getMessage());
    }
}
```

**RequestAiMoveInputData** (record): (GameState state, AiStrategy strategy)
**RequestAiMoveInputBoundary**: void execute(RequestAiMoveInputData)
**RequestAiMoveOutputData** (record): (GameState updatedState)
**RequestAiMoveOutputBoundary**: prepareSuccessView(RequestAiMoveOutputData), prepareFailView(String)
**RequestAiMoveInteractor**:
```java
public void execute(RequestAiMoveInputData inputData) {
    if (inputData.state().isGameOver()) {
        presenter.prepareFailView("cannot request an AI move after the game is over");
        return;
    }
    Position move = inputData.strategy().selectMove(inputData.state().board(), inputData.state().config(), inputData.state().currentTurn());
    presenter.prepareSuccessView(new RequestAiMoveOutputData(inputData.state().applyMove(move)));
}
```

package com.tictactoe.game.adapters;

public final class GameController
    implements StartNewGameOutputBoundary, MakeHumanMoveOutputBoundary, RequestAiMoveOutputBoundary {

    private static final Mark AI_MARK = GameState.STARTING_MARK.other();

    private final GameView view;
    private final StartNewGameInputBoundary startNewGame;
    private final MakeHumanMoveInputBoundary makeHumanMove;
    private final RequestAiMoveInputBoundary requestAiMove;
    private final AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory;
    private final UiScheduler uiScheduler;

    private GameState currentState;
    private NewGameRequest lastRequest;
    private Optional<AiStrategy> aiStrategy = Optional.empty();
    private GameState pendingAiBase;

    public GameController(GameView view, UiScheduler uiScheduler, AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory) {
        this.view = view;
        this.uiScheduler = uiScheduler;
        this.aiStrategyFactory = aiStrategyFactory;
        this.startNewGame = new StartNewGameInteractor(this);
        this.makeHumanMove = new MakeHumanMoveInteractor(this);
        this.requestAiMove = new RequestAiMoveInteractor(this);
    }

    public void onStartGameRequested(NewGameRequest request) {
        this.lastRequest = request;
        this.aiStrategy = request.mode() == GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI
            ? Optional.of(aiStrategyFactory.create(request.aiDifficulty().orElseThrow()))
            : Optional.empty();
        startNewGame.execute(new StartNewGameInputData(request));
    }

    public void onCellClicked(int row, int column) {
        if (currentState.isGameOver() || isAiTurn()) {
            return;
        }
        makeHumanMove.execute(new MakeHumanMoveInputData(currentState, new Position(row, column)));
    }

    public void onRestartRequested() {
        startNewGame.execute(new StartNewGameInputData(lastRequest));
    }

    private boolean isAiTurn() { ... same ... }

    private void requestAiMoveAsync() {
        this.pendingAiBase = currentState;
        AiStrategy strategy = aiStrategy.orElseThrow();
        uiScheduler.runInBackground(() ->
            requestAiMove.execute(new RequestAiMoveInputData(pendingAiBase, strategy)));
    }

    private void render() { ... same ... }

    @Override
    public void prepareSuccessView(StartNewGameOutputData outputData) {
        currentState = outputData.gameState();
        render();
    }

    @Override
    public void prepareSuccessView(MakeHumanMoveOutputData outputData) {
        currentState = outputData.updatedState();
        render();
        if (isAiTurn()) {
            requestAiMoveAsync();
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void prepareSuccessView(RequestAiMoveOutputData outputData) {
        GameState updated = outputData.updatedState();
        GameState base = pendingAiBase;
        uiScheduler.runOnUiThread(() -> {
            if (currentState.equals(base)) {
                currentState = updated;
                render();
            }
        });
    }

    @Override
    public void prepareFailView(String error) {
        view.displayError(error);
    }
}
```

```java
package com.tictactoe.game.use_case;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.mockito.Mockito.verify;
import com.tictactoe.game.NewGameRequest;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.GameConfig;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.GameMode;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.GameState;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.InProgress;
import com.tictactoe.game.domain.Mark;
import java.util.Optional;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.ExtendWith;
import org.mockito.ArgumentCaptor;
import org.mockito.Mock;
import org.mockito.junit.jupiter.MockitoExtension;

@ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class)
class StartNewGameInteractorTest {
    @Mock private StartNewGameOutputBoundary presenter;
    private StartNewGameInteractor interactor;
    @BeforeEach void setUp() { interactor = new StartNewGameInteractor(presenter); }

    @Test
    void executeCreatesGameWithConfiguredBoardSizeAndWinLength() {
        GameConfig config = new GameConfig(4, 3);
        interactor.execute(new StartNewGameInputData(new NewGameRequest(config, GameMode.TWO_PLAYER, Optional.empty())));

        ArgumentCaptor<StartNewGameOutputData> captor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(StartNewGameOutputData.class);
        verify(presenter).prepareSuccessView(captor.capture());
        GameState state = captor.getValue().gameState();
        assertThat(state.config()).isEqualTo(config);
        assertThat(state.board().emptyPositions()).hasSize(16);
    }

    @Test
    void executeStartsWithEmptyBoardXsTurnAndInProgressStatus() {
        GameConfig config = new GameConfig(3, 3);
        interactor.execute(new StartNewGameInputData(new NewGameRequest(config, GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI, Optional.empty())));

        ArgumentCaptor<StartNewGameOutputData> captor = ArgumentCaptor.forClass(StartNewGameOutputData.class);
        verify(presenter).prepareSuccessView(captor.capture());
        GameState state = captor.getValue().gameState();
        assertThat(state.currentTurn()).isEqualTo(Mark.X);
        assertThat(state.status()).isInstanceOf(InProgress.class);
    }
}
```

    @Test
    void executeValidMove_PreparesSuccessViewWithUpdatedState() {
        interactor.execute(new MakeHumanMoveInputData(GameState.newGame(CONFIG_3X3), new Position(0, 0)));
        ArgumentCaptor<MakeHumanMoveOutputData> captor = ...;
        verify(presenter).prepareSuccessView(captor.capture());
        GameState next = captor.getValue().updatedState();
        assertThat(next.board().get(new Position(0,0))).contains(Mark.X);
        assertThat(next.currentTurn()).isEqualTo(Mark.O);
    }

    @Test
    void executeGameAlreadyOver_PreparesFailView() {
        GameState over = ...winning sequence...;
        interactor.execute(new MakeHumanMoveInputData(over, new Position(2, 2)));
        verify(presenter).prepareFailView(anyString());
        verify(presenter, never()).prepareSuccessView(any());
    }

    @Test
    void executeCellOccupied_PreparesFailView() {
        GameState state = GameState.newGame(CONFIG_3X3).applyMove(new Position(0,0));
        interactor.execute(new MakeHumanMoveInputData(state, new Position(0,0)));
        verify(presenter).prepareFailView(anyString());
        verify(presenter, never()).prepareSuccessView(any());
    }
}

import com.tictactoe.domain.GameState;

import com.tictactoe.domain.ai.AiStrategy;
import com.tictactoe.domain.exception.InvalidMoveException;

public final class RequestAiMoveUseCase {

    public GameState execute(GameState state, AiStrategy strategy) {
        if (state.isGameOver()) {
            throw new InvalidMoveException("cannot request an AI move after the game is over");
        }

        Position move = strategy.selectMove(state.board(), state.config(), state.currentTurn());
        return state.applyMove(move);
    }
}

com.tictactoe.game.use_case.MakeHumanMoveUseCase;\nimport com.tictactoe.game.use_case.RequestAiMoveUseCase;\nimport com.tictactoe.game.use_case.StartNewGameUseCase;\nimport com.tictactoe.game.domain.GameMode;\nimport com.tictactoe.game.domain.GameState;\nimport com.tictactoe.game.domain.Mark;\nimport com.tictactoe.game.domain.Position;\nimport com.tictactoe.game.domain.exception.InvalidMoveException;\nimport java.util.Optional;\n\npublic final class GameController {\n\n    private static final Mark AI_MARK = GameState.STARTING_MARK.other();\n\n    private final GameView view;\n    private final StartNewGameUseCase startNewGameUseCase;\n    private final MakeHumanMoveUseCase makeHumanMoveUseCase;\n    private final RequestAiMoveUseCase requestAiMoveUseCase;\n    private final AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory;\n    private final UiScheduler uiScheduler;\n\n    private GameState currentState;\n    private NewGameRequest lastRequest;\n    private Optional<AiStrategy> aiStrategy = Optional.empty();\n\n    public GameController(\n            GameView view,\n            StartNewGameUseCase startNewGameUseCase,\n            MakeHumanMoveUseCase makeHumanMoveUseCase,\n            RequestAiMoveUseCase requestAiMoveUseCase,\n            AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory,\n            UiScheduler uiScheduler) {\n        this.view = view;\n        this.startNewGameUseCase = startNewGameUseCase;\n        this.makeHumanMoveUseCase = makeHumanMoveUseCase;\n        this.requestAiMoveUseCase = requestAiMoveUseCase;\n        this.aiStrategyFactory = aiStrategyFactory;\n        this.uiScheduler = uiScheduler;\n    }\n\n    public void onStartGameRequested(NewGameRequest request) {\n        this.lastRequest = request;\n        this.currentState = startNewGameUseCase.execute(request);\n        this.aiStrategy = request.mode() == GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI\n            ? Optional.of(aiStrategyFactory.create(request.aiDifficulty().orElseThrow()))\n            : Optional.empty();\n        render();\n    }\n\n    public void onCellClicked(int row, int column) {\n        if (currentState.isGameOver() || isAiTurn()) {\n            return;\n        }\n\n        try {\n            currentState = makeHumanMoveUseCase.execute(currentState, new Position(row, column));\n        } catch (InvalidMoveException e) {\n            view.displayError(e.getMessage());\n            return;\n        }\n        render();\n\n        if (isAiTurn()) {\n            requestAiMoveAsync();\n        }\n    }\n\n    public void onRestartRequested() {\n        currentState = startNewGameUseCase.execute(lastRequest);\n        render();\n    }\n\n    private boolean isAiTurn() {\n        return !currentState.isGameOver()\n            && lastRequest.mode() == GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI\n            && currentState.currentTurn() == AI_MARK;\n    }\n\n    private void requestAiMoveAsync() {\n        GameState stateBeforeAiMove = currentState;\n        AiStrategy strategy = aiStrategy.orElseThrow();\n        uiScheduler.runInBackground(() -> {\n            GameState updated = requestAiMoveUseCase.execute(stateBeforeAiMove, strategy);\n            uiScheduler.runOnUiThread(() -> {\n                // discard a stale result if the session moved on (e.g. a restart) while\n                // this AI move was being computed in the background\n                if (currentState.equals(stateBeforeAiMove)) {\n                    currentState = updated;\n                    render();\n                }\n            });\n        });\n    }\n\n    private void render() {\n        view.displayBoard(GameViewModelMapper.toBoardViewModel(currentState));\n        view.displayStatus(GameViewModelMapper.toStatusViewModel(currentState));\n    }\n}",

Here's how the code is organized after the refactor.

## The use_case boundary pattern

Each of the three use cases is now five classes in `com.tictactoe.game.use_case`, mirroring CAWithBuilder:

**StartNewGame**
- `StartNewGameInputBoundary` — the interface the controller calls (`execute(StartNewGameInputData)`)
- `StartNewGameInputData` — a record carrying `NewGameRequest`
- `StartNewGameInteractor` — the logic: builds a fresh `GameState` via `GameStateFactory.newGame(...)` and hands it to the presenter
- `StartNewGameOutputBoundary` — the interface the interactor calls back into (`prepareSuccessView(StartNewGameOutputData)`, `prepareFailView(String)`)
- `StartNewGameOutputData` — a record carrying the resulting `GameState`

**MakeHumanMove** and **RequestAiMove** follow the same shape. Their output data carries `updatedState` instead of `gameState`.

## The flow / direction of dependencies

```
UI event ──> GameController ──> *InputBoundary.execute(InputData)
                                  │
                                  └──> *Interactor ──> *OutputBoundary.prepareSuccessView(OutputData)
                                        (uses domain GameState)
```

Key changes vs. before:
- The controller no longer calls a concrete `*UseCase.execute(...)` and reads a returned `GameState`. It now depends only on the **input boundary interfaces** and receives results through the **output boundary callbacks**.
- `GameController` implements all three `OutputBoundary` interfaces — it acts as the **presenter** for now (`prepareSuccessView` stores the new state and calls `render()`; `prepareFailView` calls `view.displayError`). A dedicated Presenter/State/ViewModel/View was deferred, so the controller plays that role.
- **Wiring cycle broken:** the controller needs the interactors, and the interactors need the controller as their presenter. Since the interactors now take the presenter in their constructor, the controller just builds `new StartNewGameInteractor(this)` internally — no circular reference at construction.
- **Async stays sane:** `RequestAiMoveInteractor` runs on a background thread and reports via `prepareSuccessView(RequestAiMoveOutputData)`. The controller checks `currentState.equals(pendingAiBase)` inside `prepareSuccessView` (dispatched to the UI thread) so a stale AI result after a restart is discarded.

## Where things live

```
com.tictactoe.game
├── use_case/      ← the 3 × 5 boundary classes (this refactor)
├── adapters/      ← GameController (implements the output boundaries), GameControllerBuilder, view model mapping, GameView
├── ai/            ← strategies + AiStrategyFactory (a sub-capability)
├── domain/        ← GameState, Board, Mark, etc. + domain/exception
└── NewGameRequest
com.tictactoe.framework(.ui)   ← Swing delivery mechanism (Main, MainFrame, panels)
```

`GameControllerBuilder` no longer exposes the three use cases (no more `startNewGameUseCase(...)` override methods) — the controller wires them itself; the builder only requires `view` and `uiScheduler` and defaults `AiStrategyFactory`.

## Why it matters

- Dependencies point inward: `adapters` → `use_case` → `domain`, satisfying the Clean Architecture dependency rule.
- The interactors are now independently testable against a mocked `OutputBoundary` (see `StartNewGameInteractorTest` etc.), asserting on captured output data instead of the old "call and catch a thrown exception" style.

Here's my analysis of the test suite (23 classes, 107 tests) and a proposed cleanup, ordered by value.

## Inventory
- **domain (7):** Board, GameConfig, GameState, LineGenerator, Mark, Position, WinChecker
- **ai (6):** AiStrategyFactory, BoardEvaluator, EasyAiStrategy, MinimaxAiStrategy, MoveOrderer, RandomAiStrategy
- **adapters (6):** GameControllerBuilder, GameController, GameViewDecorator, GameViewModelMapper, NewGameRequestFactory, WinEffectGameView
- **use_case (3):** MakeHumanMove, RequestAiMove, StartNewGame interactors

## Issues found

### 1. Duplicated board fixtures (biggest win)
The exact same move sequences are hand-written all over:
- **Win by X top row** `(0,0)X (1,0)O (0,1)X (1,1)O (0,2)X` appears in `GameStateTest` (×2), `GameViewModelMapperTest` (×2), `GameControllerTest` (×2), `MakeHumanMoveInteractorTest`, `RequestAiMoveInteractorTest`, `WinCheckerTest`.
- **Draw grid** `X O X / X X O / O X O` appears in `GameStateTest`, `GameViewModelMapperTest`, `GameControllerTest`, `BoardEvaluatorTest`, `WinCheckerTest`.

Proposal: a shared test helper (e.g. `com.tictactoe.game.testutil.GameFixtures`) with `startingState(config)`, `wonByXState()`, `drawnState()`. Removes ~40 duplicated lines and makes intent obvious.

### 2. Redundant same-package imports
`AiStrategyFactoryTest` imports `com.tictactoe.game.ai.AiStrategy/EasyAiStrategy/MinimaxAiStrategy/RandomAiStrategy` — all in the test's own package (a Phase B leftover). Delete 4 imports.

### 3. `GameControllerTest` boilerplate
Every test repeats `GameView view = mock(...); GameController controller = newController(view); controller.onStartGameRequested(twoPlayerRequest());`. A `@BeforeEach` (matching the interactor tests' style) would remove ~25 lines. The immediate/capturing scheduler scaffolding is also re-implemented in two classes and could be a shared helper.

### 4. Stale / overlapping builder test
`GameControllerBuilderTest.buildWithOnlyRequiredDependenciesWiresTheUseCasesAndFactory` references "use cases" that no longer live in the builder (the controller wires them now). It also re-tests controller behavior already covered by `GameControllerTest` (start + place a move). Rename to reflect it verifies an end-to-end working graph, and consider whether the behavior half is redundant.

### 5. Flaky timing tests
`MinimaxAiStrategyTest.respondsWithinBoundedTimeOnLargerBoard_6x6` / `_9x9` assert `elapsedMillis < 10_000`. Wall-clock assertions are flaky on slow/loaded CI. Consider relaxing or removing the timing check (keep the "returns a legal move" assertion).

### 6. Naming inconsistency (needs a decision)
AGENTS.md + the CAWithBuilder reference mandate `Method_Condition_Expectation` (e.g. `execute_ValidState_PresentsUpdatedState`), and the 3 new interactor tests follow it — but the domain/ai/adapters tests use camelCase (`applyMoveByCurrentPlayerAdvancesTurnToOtherMark`, `onCellClickedAppliesHumanMoveAndRendersUpdatedBoard`). Options: (a) rename ~60 camelCase tests to the underscore style, or (b) accept camelCase for the older suites. This is the most invasive item.

### 7. Boundary-vs-domain overlap
`StartNewGameInteractorTest` largely re-tests `GameState.newGame` (`GameStateTest`), and `MakeHumanMoveInteractorTest` re-tests `applyMove`. Some overlap is expected at the boundary, but I'd trim so each interactor test focuses on what *it* adds (wiring, error→fail-view translation) and let the domain tests own move mechanics.

## Suggested priority
1. Do now (low risk): **#2** imports, **#4** builder test name, **#5** timing.
2. High value: **#1** fixtures, **#3** `@BeforeEach`.
3. Decision needed: **#6** naming, **#7** overlap.

**1. Interactor tests re-verify domain mechanics already covered by `GameStateTest`:**

- `MakeHumanMoveInteractorTest` (3) — `applyMove`, occupied-cell throw, game-over throw are all direct duplicates of `GameStateTest`. New behavior: exception → `prepareFailView`. → **cut to 2** (1 success + 1 fail; the two fail cases are the same translation path) (save 1).
- `RequestAiMoveInteractorTest` (2) — success path re-tests `applyMove`; the game-over guard (`prepareFailView` before consulting the strategy) is genuinely interactor logic. → **cut to 1** (keep the guard test; optionally verify `strategy.selectMove` via Mockito instead of asserting the resulting board) (save 1).

**3. `NewGameRequestFactoryTest.createPropagatesInvalidGameConfigException...`** — duplicates `GameConfigTest`'s win-length validation; the factory just passes through. → **cut** (save 1).

## What I'd NOT cut
- **`GameControllerTest` (11)** — unique behavior through the controller (AI scheduling, stale-result discard, restart).
- **`GameViewModelMapperTest` (5)** — tests the mapper itself, not the domain.
- **`WinCheckerTest` (13), AI tests, decorator/effect tests** — self-contained.
- **`GameStateTest` immutability test** (`applyMoveReturnsNewInstance...`) — unique.

Net: **107 → ~102** (~5% cut). The suite is small, so that's the honest ceiling — deeper cuts would remove real boundary coverage.

**Differences / possible updates:**

1. **Package naming**: tictactoe uses `com.tictactoe` prefix; CAWithBuilder uses bare top-level packages (`account`, `app`, `framework`, etc.). This was already noted as deferred scope ("package naming (drop com.tictactoe)").

2. **`NewGameRequest.java` sits directly in `game/`** — a shared request object used by the adapters and use cases. In CAWithBuilder, input data carries primitives and the use case doesn't depend on a shared request record. Hmm. The NewGameRequest is basically the InputData for StartNewGame. Interesting: StartNewGameInputData wraps NewGameRequest (a record with config, mode, aiDifficulty). In CAWithBuilder, SignupInputData holds the primitives (username, password, email). So tictactoe could flatten NewGameRequest into StartNewGameInputData and have the controller (NewGameRequestFactory) build InputData directly. Actually NewGameRequestFactory creates NewGameRequest; GameController.onStartGameRequested(NewGameRequest) takes it. This is a design mismatch vs CAWithBuilder: the Controller takes the "request" and passes it to the InputData. In CAWithBuilder the LoginController builds LoginInputData itself. So the update: fold NewGameRequest into StartNewGameInputData; NewGameRequestFactory becomes the request-building part of the controller or the controller builds input data directly.

3. **Missing Presenter/State/ViewModel/View per use case**: CAWithBuilder has, per capability: Controller, Presenter, State, View, ViewModel, use_case boundaries. Tictactoe has a single GameController implementing all three OutputBoundaries, one GameView, and a GameViewModelMapper producing view models. This was previously identified as deferred scope ("Presenter/State/ViewModel/View rework").

4. **Missing `app/AppBuilder`**: CAWithBuilder has `app/AppBuilder.java` + `app/Main.java` that wires the whole application. Tictactoe has `GameControllerBuilder` in adapters and `framework/Main.java`. The rework to AppBuilder was also deferred.

5. **`user/` domain entity**: CAWithBuilder has `user/User`, `UserFactory`, `CommonUser`, `CommonUserFactory` at the top-level capability, shared across signup/login/change_password. Tictactoe's shared domain is `game/domain/` with `GameStateFactory`. Equivalent-ish (already there).

6. **data_access/**: CAWithBuilder has `data_access/` with DAOs. Tictactoe: N/A (nothing persisted) — already noted.

7. **use_case subpackage naming**: tictactoe uses `game/use_case/` at the game capability level with all three use cases' boundaries inside. CAWithBuilder nests `use_case` inside each capability subfolder (`account/signup/use_case`). The AGENTS.md says "capability folder contains its use_case subpackage". In tictactoe, use_case is at the `game` capability level and contains 3 use cases. In CAWithBuilder, the granularity is finer: each use case is its own capability folder (`account/signup`, `account/change_password`, `authentication/login`), each with its own use_case. So for tictactoe the closer match would be `game/start_new_game/use_case/`, `game/make_human_move/use_case/`, `game/request_ai_move/use_case/`, with controllers/presenters/view models in each capability folder. This is a structural difference worth noting.

8. **View/ViewModel per use case**: In CAWithBuilder, each capability has its own View interface, ViewModel, State, Presenter. Tictactoe: single GameView, single mapper, viewmodels in adapters/viewmodel. The Presenter/State/ViewModel rework is deferred, as noted.

9. **Tests**: CAWithBuilder has interactor tests only (per use_case). Tictactoe has full test coverage everywhere — that's fine/better.

So the "possible updates" list, comparing:

A. **Package naming**: drop `com.tictactoe` root package to match bare capability packages. (Previously deferred.)

B. **Use-case granularity**: restructure `game/use_case/` (one shared package) into per-use-case capability folders: `game/start_new_game/` (controller, presenter, state, view, viewmodel, use_case), `game/make_human_move/`, `game/request_ai_move/`. Currently the interactors/boundaries are all in one `use_case` package.

C. **Fold NewGameRequest into StartNewGameInputData**: adapters pass primitives; NewGameRequestFactory moves into the controller (or becomes the controller). This removes the shared request record that neither the interactor nor CAWithBuilder pattern has.

D. **Presenter/State/ViewModel/View split per use case**: CAWithBuilder: each use case has Presenter + State + ViewModel + View; GameController currently implements all output boundaries and renders directly. This is the big deferred rework.

E. **AppBuilder**: move wiring from GameControllerBuilder/adapters + framework/Main into an `app/` package with an `AppBuilder`.

F. **data_access/**: N/A.

Builds the input data from\n * primitives (as the CAWithBuilder controllers do) and remembers the last\n * input so the view can request a restart with the same settings.\n */\npublic class StartNewGameController {\n\n    private final StartNewGameInputBoundary startNewGameUseCase;\n    private final AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory;\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n\n    private StartNewGameInputData lastInput;\n\n    public StartNewGameController(\n            StartNewGameInputBoundary startNewGameUseCase,\n            AiStrategyFactory aiStrategyFactory,\n            GameViewModel gameViewModel) {\n        this.startNewGameUseCase = startNewGameUseCase;\n        this.aiStrategyFactory = aiStrategyFactory;\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n    }\n\n    public void execute(int boardSize, int winLength, GameMode mode,\n                        Optional<AiDifficulty> aiDifficulty) {\n        final StartNewGameInputData inputData = new StartNewGameInputData(\n                new GameConfig(boardSize, winLength), mode, aiDifficulty);\n        this.lastInput = inputData;\n\n        final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n        state.setMode(mode);\n        state.setAiStrategy(mode == GameMode.HUMAN_VS_AI\n                ? Optional.of(aiStrategyFactory.create(aiDifficulty.orElseThrow()))\n                : Optional.empty());\n\n        startNewGameUseCase.execute(inputData);\n    }\n\n    public void restart() {\n        startNewGameUseCase.execute(lastInput);\n    }\n}",

Updates the shared game\n * view model and fires a property change so the view re-renders; when the\n * move leaves the board on the AI's turn, hands off to the AI move request\n * (wired by the AppBuilder).\n */\npublic class MakeHumanMovePresenter implements MakeHumanMoveOutputBoundary {\n\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n    private final Runnable requestAiMove;\n\n    public MakeHumanMovePresenter(GameViewModel gameViewModel, Runnable requestAiMove) {\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n        this.requestAiMove = requestAiMove;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareSuccessView(MakeHumanMoveOutputData outputData) {\n        final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n        state.setCurrentGameState(outputData.updatedState());\n        state.setBoard(GameViewModelMapper.toBoardViewModel(outputData.updatedState()));\n        state.setStatus(GameViewModelMapper.toStatusViewModel(outputData.updatedState()));\n        state.setError(null);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n\n        if (state.isAiTurn()) {\n            requestAiMove.run();\n        }\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareFailView(String error) {\n        final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n        state.setError(error);\n        gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n    }\n}",

{
  "content": "package game.request_ai_move;\n\nimport game.GameState;\nimport game.GameViewModel;\nimport game.GameViewModelMapper;\nimport game.request_ai_move.use_case.RequestAiMoveOutputBoundary;\nimport game.request_ai_move.use_case.RequestAiMoveOutputData;\nimport framework.UiScheduler;\n\n/**\n * The Presenter for the Request AI Move Use Case. Applies the AI move on the\n * UI thread, discarding the result if the session moved on (e.g. a restart)\n * while the move was being computed in the background.\n */\npublic class RequestAiMovePresenter implements RequestAiMoveOutputBoundary {\n\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n    private final UiScheduler uiScheduler;\n\n    public RequestAiMovePresenter(GameViewModel gameViewModel, UiScheduler uiScheduler) {\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n        this.uiScheduler = uiScheduler;\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareSuccessView(RequestAiMoveOutputData outputData) {\n        uiScheduler.runOnUiThread(() -> {\n            final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n            if (!state.isStaleAiResult(outputData.updatedState())) {\n                state.setCurrentGameState(outputData.updatedState());\n                state.setBoard(GameViewModelMapper.toBoardViewModel(outputData.updatedState()));\n                state.setStatus(GameViewModelMapper.toStatusViewModel(outputData.updatedState()));\n                state.setError(null);\n                gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n            }\n        });\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void prepareFailView(String error) {\n        uiScheduler.runOnUiThread(() -> {\n            final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n            state.setError(error);\n            gameViewModel.firePropertyChanged();\n        });\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/game/request_ai_move/RequestAiMovePresenter.java"
}

{
  "content": "package game.request_ai_move;\n\nimport game.GameState;\nimport game.GameViewModel;\nimport game.ai.AiStrategy;\nimport game.request_ai_move.use_case.RequestAiMoveInputBoundary;\nimport game.request_ai_move.use_case.RequestAiMoveInputData;\nimport framework.UiScheduler;\n\n/**\n * The Controller for the Request AI Move Use Case. Runs the use case in the\n * background on a snapshot of the current session, marking that snapshot so\n * the presenter can discard stale results after a restart.\n */\npublic class RequestAiMoveController {\n\n    private final RequestAiMoveInputBoundary requestAiMoveUseCase;\n    private final GameViewModel gameViewModel;\n    private final UiScheduler uiScheduler;\n\n    public RequestAiMoveController(\n            RequestAiMoveInputBoundary requestAiMoveUseCase,\n            GameViewModel gameViewModel,\n            UiScheduler uiScheduler) {\n        this.requestAiMoveUseCase = requestAiMoveUseCase;\n        this.gameViewModel = gameViewModel;\n        this.uiScheduler = uiScheduler;\n    }\n\n    public void execute() {\n        final GameState state = gameViewModel.getState();\n        state.setPendingAiBase(state.getCurrentGameState());\n        final AiStrategy strategy = state.getAiStrategy().orElseThrow();\n\n        uiScheduler.runInBackground(() -> {\n            requestAiMoveUseCase.execute(new RequestAiMoveInputData(\n                    state.getPendingAiBase(), strategy));\n        });\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/main/java/game/request_ai_move/RequestAiMoveController.java"
}

Design details:

**ImmediateUiScheduler:**
```java
package game.testutil;
public final class ImmediateUiScheduler implements UiScheduler {
    @Override public void runInBackground(Runnable task) { task.run(); }
    @Override public void runOnUiThread(Runnable task) { task.run(); }
}
```

**CapturingUiScheduler:**
```java
package game.testutil;
public final class CapturingUiScheduler implements UiScheduler {
    private final List<Runnable> backgroundTasks = new ArrayList<>();
    private final List<Runnable> uiTasks = new ArrayList<>();
    @Override public void runInBackground(Runnable task) { backgroundTasks.add(task); }
    @Override public void runOnUiThread(Runnable task) { uiTasks.add(task); }
    public void runNextBackgroundTask() { backgroundTasks.remove(0).run(); }
    public void runNextUiTask() { uiTasks.remove(0).run(); }
    public boolean hasUiTasks() { return !uiTasks.isEmpty(); }
}
```

The presenter reads state AFTER updating with outputData.updatedState(). isAiTurn checks state.mode + currentGameState. {
  "content": "package game.testutil;\n\nimport framework.UiScheduler;\nimport java.util.ArrayList;\nimport java.util.List;\n\n/**\n * Captures background and UI tasks so a test can run them manually, one at a\n * time, to simulate a pending AI move or a queued UI update.\n */\npublic final class CapturingUiScheduler implements UiScheduler {\n\n    private final List<Runnable> backgroundTasks = new ArrayList<>();\n    private final List<Runnable> uiTasks = new ArrayList<>();\n\n    @Override\n    public void runInBackground(Runnable task) {\n        backgroundTasks.add(task);\n    }\n\n    @Override\n    public void runOnUiThread(Runnable task) {\n        uiTasks.add(task);\n    }\n\n    public void runNextBackgroundTask() {\n        backgroundTasks.remove(0).run();\n    }\n\n    public void runNextUiTask() {\n        uiTasks.remove(0).run();\n    }\n\n    public int pendingBackgroundTasks() {\n        return backgroundTasks.size();\n    }\n\n    public int pendingUiTasks() {\n        return uiTasks.size();\n    }\n}",
  "filePath": "/Users/pgries/Projects/ca_examples/tictactoe/src/test/java/game/testutil/CapturingUiScheduler.java"

16:   (branch off the previous branch) when several PRs will merge to `main`
17:   sequentially.
18: - Push to the user's fork; open PRs against upstream with `gh`:
19:   `gh pr create --repo <upstream> --base main --head <fork>:<branch>`.
20: - Open a PR to `main`, **Rebase and merge** to keep history linear.
21: - The user reviews and approves/merges the PR themselves.
22: - Branches are **kept** (not deleted) as teaching artifacts.
23: - Use `gh` for PRs, issues, and checks.
24: 
25: ## Architecture
26: 
27: - **Clean Architecture**, package-by-capability.
28: - Structure: capability folder contains its `use_case` subpackage; layers live
29:   inside capabilities rather than top-level layers.
30: - Example layout:
31:   - `account/signup/use_case`
32:   - `account/change_password/use_case`
33:   - `authentication/login/use_case`
34:   - `user/` (shared domain entity)
35:   - `data_access/`, `framework/`, `app/`
36: - Build a `CommonUser`/`CommonUserFactory` style entity for domain models.
37: - Each use case gets a boundary set under its `use_case` package:
38:   `InputBoundary`, `InputData`, `Interactor`, `OutputBoundary`, `OutputData`.
39:   Interactors are `void` and receive the `OutputBoundary` in their
40:   constructor; adapter-side controllers implement the `OutputBoundary` and
41:   wire the interactors internally.
42: 
43: ## Testing
44: 
45: - **JUnit 5 + Mockito** (`mockito-junit-jupiter`).
46: - Build the class under test (e.g. interactor) in `@BeforeEach`, after mocks
47:   are injected.
48: - Use real entities/implementations where possible; mock only boundaries
49:   (DAOs, presenters).
50: - Assert on the real effect (e.g. captured saved user), not just method calls.
51: - Boundary/interactor tests verify **wiring** (presenter called / never
52:   called, what was passed) without re-asserting domain mechanics covered by
53:   domain tests; drop tests that fully duplicate lower-layer coverage (one
54:   fail path suffices when cases share the same translation).
55: - Extract repeated fixtures into a shared test helper
56:   (e.g. `com.tictactoe.game.testutil.GameFixtures`) instead of duplicating
57:   board/state-building sequences in each test class.
58: - Run `mvn clean test` — incremental compilation can report false positives.
59:   `mvn` output is the source of truth; ignore stale editor/LSP diagnostics
60:   on in-progress branches.
61: - Test names: `Method_Condition_Expectation` style.
62: 
63: ## Naming conventions
64: 
65: - **Types**: `PascalCase` (`SignupInteractor`).
66: - **Methods/fields**: `camelCase`.
67: - **Constants**: `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
68: - **Packages**: all lowercase; capability-based, no underscores/camelCase.
69: - **Branches**: `kebab-case`, short and descriptive (`add-conversation-log`).
70: - **Commits**: Conventional Commit types (see above).
71: 
72: ## Environment
73: 
74: - macOS, zsh shell.
75: - **BSD `sed`** — does not support GNU `\b` word boundaries; use `[^...]`
76:   classes or alternate tools.
77: 
78: ## AI-usage tracking
79: 
80: - Commit the live session transcript (`conversations/<session>.md`) as the
81:   durable record of AI-assisted work; git history is the per-commit record.
82: - To resume context, use opencode's `/sessions` (or `/compact`), **not** by
83:   loading the transcript file back in as context.
84: 
85: ## Build
86: 
87: - Maven project (`pom.xml`), Java. Verify with `mvn clean test`.

(End of file - total 87 lines)
</content>
```

# CAWithBuilder alignment: capability folders + request folding

Date: 2026-08-18

## Objective

Re-compare tictactoe against CAWithBuilder and close the two mechanical
deltas:

1. Per-use-case capability folders (each capability owns its `use_case/`).
2. Fold the `NewGameRequest` middleman: controllers take primitives and
   build `InputData` themselves, as CAWithBuilder controllers do.

## Changes

### #2 Per-use-case capability folders

Moved (git mv + package fix) the shared `game/use_case/` into:

- `game/start_new_game/use_case` — StartNewGame boundaries + interactor

Yes — `game/domain/` is the entity layer. It holds the entities (domain model) and nothing that depends on outside layers:

- **Entities**: `GameState` (the `CommonUser`-style root entity, built via `GameStateFactory`), `Board`, `Mark`, `Position`, `GameConfig`, `GameStatus` + sealed variants (`InProgress`, `Win`, `Draw`)
- **Pure domain logic**: `WinChecker`, `LineGenerator` (helpers that serve the entities)
- **Domain values/enums**: `GameMode`, `AiDifficulty`, exceptions

Note the deliberate naming clash: the presentation bean `game.GameState` is *not* an entity — it's the view-model state living in `game/`, while the entity is `game.domain.GameState` (fully qualified inside the bean).
